# Microsoft Azure Maintenance management client library for .NET

This library supports managing Microsoft Azure Maintenance resources.

This library follows the [new Azure SDK guidelines](https://azure.github.io/azure-sdk/general_introduction.html), and provides many core capabilities:

    - Support MSAL.NET, Azure.Identity is out of box for supporting MSAL.NET.
    - Support [OpenTelemetry](https://opentelemetry.io/) for distributed tracing.
    - HTTP pipeline with custom policies.
    - Better error-handling.
    - Support uniform telemetry across all languages.

## Getting started 

### Install the package

Install the Microsoft Azure Maintenance management library for .NET with [NuGet](https://www.nuget.org/):

```dotnetcli
dotnet add package Azure.ResourceManager.Maintenance
```

### Prerequisites

* You must have an [Microsoft Azure subscription](https://azure.microsoft.com/free/dotnet/).

### Authenticate the Client

To create an authenticated client and start interacting with Microsoft Azure resources, see the [quickstart guide here](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/blob/main/doc/dev/mgmt_quickstart.md).

## Key concepts

Key concepts of the Microsoft Azure SDK for .NET can be found [here](https://azure.github.io/azure-sdk/dotnet_introduction.html)..

## Documentation

Documentation is available to help you learn how to use this package:

- [Quickstart](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/blob/main/doc/dev/mgmt_quickstart.md).
- [API References](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/?view=azure-dotnet).
- [Authentication](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/blob/main/sdk/identity/Azure.Identity/README.md).

## Examples

Code samples for using the management library for .NET can be found in the following locations
- [.NET Management Library Code Samples](https://aka.ms/azuresdk-net-mgmt-samples)

## Troubleshooting

-   File an issue via [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/issues).
-   Check [previous questions](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/tagged/azure+.net) or ask new ones on Stack Overflow using Azure and .NET tags.

## Next steps

For more information about Microsoft Azure SDK, see [this website](https://azure.github.io/azure-sdk/).

## Contributing

For details on contributing to this repository, see the [contributing
guide][cg].

This project welcomes contributions and suggestions. Most contributions
require you to agree to a Contributor License Agreement (CLA) declaring
that you have the right to, and actually do, grant us the rights to use
your contribution. For details, visit <https://cla.microsoft.com>.

When you submit a pull request, a CLA-bot will automatically determine
whether you need to provide a CLA and decorate the PR appropriately
(for example, label, comment). Follow the instructions provided by the
bot. You'll only need to do this action once across all repositories
using our CLA.

This project has adopted the [Microsoft Open Source Code of Conduct][coc]. For
more information, see the [Code of Conduct FAQ][coc_faq] or contact
<opencode@microsoft.com> with any other questions or comments.

proposals.explanation: The seven-parameter factory has five required parameters followed by optional maintenanceConfigurationId/resourceId, and calls the same-named eight-argument overload with those identifiers before filter: default and location last.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The concrete public factory signature and forwarding body are in the handwritten Custom partial; the overload target and historical optionality claimed by comments are not independently supplied.

proposals.explanation: The wrapper classes forward continuationToken/pageSizeHint to the inner AsPages, cast each root assignment item to Models.MaintenanceConfigurationAssignmentData into a new list, and preserve each page's continuation token and raw response.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: Both complete internal adapter implementations are in handwritten Custom/CollectionResults files; sync and async implement one projection behavior.

proposals.explanation: The lazy apply-update REST client is constructed with 2025-10-01-preview and a resource-type TryGetApiVersion callback returning null on failure; Updates and ConfigurationAssignments clients use 2023-10-01-preview. Their diagnostics and clients are cached with ??=.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: These explicit lazy client/diagnostic configuration bodies are in the handwritten Custom resource-group partial, separate from request execution.

proposals.explanation: The cancellation-taking sync/async GetMaintenanceApplyUpdates methods create RequestContext, pass parsed subscription and resource-group scope to ApplyUpdateForResourceGroup collection-result objects, and use pageable wrappers with data => new MaintenanceApplyUpdateResource(Client,data).
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The public typed-page adapter bodies are handwritten in Custom source; their underlying collection-result traversal implementations are not captured.

proposals.subtype: Explicit-path apply-update creation returns a typed resource response
proposals.explanation: The sync/async creation pair calls guards for provider/type/name, builds a direct REST request with stored subscription/resource group, processes it, deserializes MaintenanceApplyUpdateData, throws RequestFailedException for a null result and returns a resource response with the raw response retained.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The complete handwritten Custom request/response methods are not simple generated operation declarations; diagnostic failure marking and rethrow are included in this behavior.

proposals.subtype: Parent-aware apply-update creation adds explicit parent path arguments
proposals.explanation: The sync/async pair guards the five path strings, creates the by-parent REST request from them and stored subscription/resource group, processes/deserializes the response, rejects null data and wraps it as MaintenanceApplyUpdateResource with the original raw response.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: These complete distinct parent-path action bodies are in handwritten Custom source, with cancellation context and diagnostic failure/rethrow implemented locally.

proposals.subtype: Explicit-path apply-update get projects a typed resource
proposals.explanation: The annotated sync/async pair guards four path arguments, uses CreateGetRequest with stored subscription/resource group, processes and deserializes the response, throws for null data, and returns a resource response while retaining the raw response.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The complete request, typed projection and diagnostic failure/rethrow bodies are in handwritten Custom source.

proposals.handwrittenRationale: Both complete options forwarding bodies are handwritten in the Custom partial; the options type's implementation is explicitly not captured.

proposals.explanation: The sync/async Exists methods send a GET request, deserialize data for status 200, assign null for 404, throw RequestFailedException for other statuses and return response.Value != null with the raw response; a 200 status alone is not the final boolean expression.

decisions.reason: The Custom partial defines a concrete seven-parameter factory overload with five required and two optional parameters, forwards to an eight-argument call with filter defaulted, and has the cited Models-namespace return type.
